FIGURE 3b — ALT4: one-column, journal-sized butterfly forest (Estuaries & Coasts)
Identical to ALT3 (weight-shaded slabs, angled annotations) EXCEPT sized for the E&C
single-column footprint (84 mm wide x <= 234 mm tall) with all lettering held at >= 8 pt
(Helvetica), plus two crowding fixes for the shrink: (1) the median marker is a short
VERTICAL HASH drawn one-sided into each survey's own slab (co-located TPS/EDSM medians
no longer overlap); (2) long covariate labels get an extra line break (after "Distance",
"Dissolved", "Emergent", "Terminal") so the y-axis strip fits one column.  Axis spacing
is uniform; the top and bottom page margins are set independently as fractions of the
axis spacing (outer_pad_frac_top / outer_pad_frac_bottom).
The survey legend is centred on the 30-day-outflow axis.  Alpha compositing means DON'T
export to EPS (transparency is lost) — PDF (vector) + TIFF (600 dpi) only.
```{r butterfly-alt4-fn}
combined_cluster_butterfly_plot_alt4 <- function(
  tps_fit_names,
  edsm_fit_names,
  fit_paths,
  tps_criteria          = NULL,
  edsm_criteria         = NULL,
  patterns_to_exclude   = character(0),
  include_regex         = "^b_",
  preferred_param_order = NULL,
  param_labels          = NULL,
  survey_colors         = c("TPS" = "#0072B2", "EDSM" = "#D55E00"),
  declutter_threshold   = 0.95,
  min_weight            = 0.01,   # drop models whose overall stacking weight is < this
  title                 = NULL,
  x_axis_label          = "Posterior beta estimate (z-score)",
  x_limits              = NULL,
  slab_scale            = 1.5,
  slab_n                = 128L,
  band_half             = 1.5,
  alpha_range           = c(0.12, 0.85),
  annot_x_gap           = 0.22,
  annot_size            = 2.85,   # geom_text size in mm; 2.85 mm ~= 8.1 pt (E&C floor is 8 pt)
  tps_annot_angle       = 45,
  edsm_annot_angle      = -45,
  tps_annot_hjust       = 0,
  edsm_annot_hjust      = 0,
  tps_annot_x           = 2.0,
  edsm_annot_x          = 2.0,
  tps_annot_y           = 0.3,
  edsm_annot_y          = 0.3,
  band_gap              = 0.4,
  show_annotations      = TRUE,   # FALSE drops the per-model number(weight) labels (alt5)
  median_tick_len       = 0.25,    # length of the median hash (band units), drawn INTO the slab
  median_tick_color     = "black",   # NULL = colour by survey; e.g. "black" for a single colour
  outer_pad_frac_top    = 0.5,    # TOP page margin as a fraction of the uniform axis spacing
  outer_pad_frac_bottom = 0.5,    # BOTTOM page margin as a fraction (0.5 = half the axis gap)
  legend_on_param       = "b_out30_z",  # covariate axis the legend is vertically centred on
  legend_x              = 0.02,   # legend left edge, panel-normalised x (0 = left)
  legend_y_nudge        = 0,      # + moves legend UP, - moves it DOWN (panel-normalised units)
  legend_swatch_alpha   = 1,    # opacity of the legend colour swatches (higher = more saturated)
  legend_text_face      = "bold",# "bold" to embolden the legend labels
  base_family           = "Helvetica",  # E&C requires Helvetica/Arial
  axis_text_y_size      = 8.5,    # pt; all lettering kept in the 8-9 pt band
                                     # ("center" or "left"); the block itself stays
                                     # right-anchored to the axis via hjust = 1
  axis_text_x_size      = 8,
  axis_title_size       = 9,
  legend_text_size      = 8,
  draws_cache           = NULL,
  method                = "stacking"
) {
  regex_excl <- if (length(patterns_to_exclude) > 0L)
    paste(patterns_to_exclude, collapse = "|") else "XXXXXXXX_NOMATCH"

  load_one <- function(nm)
    if (exists(nm, inherits = TRUE)) get(nm, inherits = TRUE) else readRDS(fit_paths[[nm]])

  build_survey_data <- function(fit_names, criteria) {
    weights   <- stacking_weights_streamed(fit_names, fit_paths, criteria, method)
    draws_raw <- vector("list", length(fit_names)); names(draws_raw) <- fit_names
    norm_list <- vector("list", length(fit_names)); names(norm_list) <- fit_names

    for (nm in fit_names) {
      df_full <- if (!is.null(draws_cache) && nm %in% names(draws_cache)) {
        draws_cache[[nm]]
      } else {
        f <- load_one(nm); d <- as_draws_df(f); rm(f); gc(verbose = FALSE); d
      }
      df       <- df_full %>% dplyr::select(-dplyr::matches(regex_excl))
      raw_cols <- names(df)[grepl(include_regex, names(df))]
      nrm      <- normalize_beta_interaction_param(raw_cols)
      draws_raw[[nm]] <- df[, raw_cols, drop = FALSE]
      norm_list[[nm]] <- setNames(nrm, raw_cols)
    }

    all_norm_params <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(norm_list, unname))))
    if (!is.null(preferred_param_order)) {
      all_norm_params <- c(
        preferred_param_order[preferred_param_order %in% all_norm_params],
        setdiff(all_norm_params, preferred_param_order)
      )
    }

    row_blocks <- list()
    for (p in all_norm_params) {
      model_idx <- which(vapply(norm_list, function(nv) p %in% nv, logical(1)))
      if (length(model_idx) == 0L) next

      w_raw <- weights[model_idx]
      total <- sum(w_raw)
      w_sub <- if (total > 0) w_raw / total else rep(0, length(w_raw))
      ord   <- order(w_sub, decreasing = TRUE)
      model_idx <- model_idx[ord]; w_sub <- w_sub[ord]; w_raw <- w_raw[ord]
      keep_n <- if (total > 0) which(cumsum(w_sub) >= declutter_threshold)[1L] else NA_integer_
      if (is.na(keep_n)) keep_n <- length(w_sub)
      model_idx <- model_idx[seq_len(keep_n)]
      w_raw     <- w_raw[seq_len(keep_n)]

      # Also drop any surviving model whose OVERALL weight is below min_weight
      # (declutter alone can keep a long tail of ~0% models within the top 95%).
      keep_mw   <- w_raw >= min_weight
      model_idx <- model_idx[keep_mw]
      w_raw     <- w_raw[keep_mw]

      for (k in seq_along(model_idx)) {
        i       <- model_idx[k]
        nm      <- fit_names[i]
        raw_col <- names(norm_list[[i]])[norm_list[[i]] == p][1L]
        row_blocks[[length(row_blocks) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
          param          = p,
          fit_name       = nm,
          model_num      = sub(".*?([0-9]+)$", "\\1", nm),
          overall_weight = w_raw[k],
          estimate       = draws_raw[[i]][[raw_col]],
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
      }
    }
    list(
      data            = if (length(row_blocks) > 0L) bind_rows(row_blocks) else data.frame(),
      all_norm_params = all_norm_params
    )
  }

  tps_res  <- build_survey_data(tps_fit_names,  tps_criteria)
  edsm_res <- build_survey_data(edsm_fit_names, edsm_criteria)

  tps_data  <- tps_res$data;  tps_data$survey  <- "TPS"
  edsm_data <- edsm_res$data; edsm_data$survey <- "EDSM"
  plot_df   <- bind_rows(tps_data, edsm_data)

  all_norm_params <- unique(c(tps_res$all_norm_params, edsm_res$all_norm_params))
  if (!is.null(preferred_param_order)) {
    all_norm_params <- c(
      preferred_param_order[preferred_param_order %in% all_norm_params],
      setdiff(all_norm_params, preferred_param_order)
    )
  }

  param_labels_disp  <- map_parameter_labels(all_norm_params, param_labels,
                                              lookup_keys = all_norm_params)
  param_label_lookup <- setNames(param_labels_disp, all_norm_params)
  plot_df$param_label <- factor(param_label_lookup[plot_df$param],
                                levels = unique(param_label_lookup[all_norm_params]))
  plot_df <- plot_df[!is.na(plot_df$param_label), ]

  ordered_present <- all_norm_params[all_norm_params %in% unique(plot_df$param)]
  K <- length(ordered_present)

  fmt_w <- function(w) ifelse(w >= 0.01, sprintf("%.0f", 100 * w), "<1")

  annot_rel <- plot_df %>%
    dplyr::group_by(param, survey, fit_name, model_num, overall_weight) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(median_x = median(estimate), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::group_by(param, survey) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(median_x, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      label_x    = ifelse(survey == "TPS", tps_annot_x, edsm_annot_x) +
                   (dplyr::row_number() - 1) * annot_x_gap,
      label_text = paste0(model_num, "(", fmt_w(overall_weight), ")")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  # Uniform, even spacing between every covariate axis: each row gets the same
  # band (row_spacing = 2*band_half + band_gap), so baselines are equally spaced.
  half_extent <- band_half
  row_spacing <- 2 * half_extent + band_gap

  pos <- setNames((K - seq_len(K)) * row_spacing, ordered_present)
  plot_df$baseline   <- pos[plot_df$param]
  annot_rel$baseline <- pos[annot_rel$param]

  annot_rel$label_y <- annot_rel$baseline +
    ifelse(annot_rel$survey == "TPS", tps_annot_y, -edsm_annot_y)

  # median hash: one-sided tick that rises INTO the model's own slab (+ for TPS,
  # - for EDSM) so co-located TPS/EDSM medians never overlap the way dots did.
  annot_rel$tick_sgn <- ifelse(annot_rel$survey == "TPS", 1, -1)

  # ── Density slabs — overall_weight carried through for weight-based shading ──
  slab_polys <- plot_df %>%
    dplyr::group_by(param, survey, fit_name, baseline, overall_weight) %>%
    dplyr::group_modify(~{
      d <- density(.x$estimate, n = slab_n, cut = 0)
      data.frame(x = d$x, dens = d$y)
    }) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(height = dens / max(dens) * slab_scale)

  slab_polys$sgn <- ifelse(slab_polys$survey == "TPS", 1, -1)
  slab_polys$grp <- paste(slab_polys$survey, slab_polys$fit_name,
                          slab_polys$param, sep = "__")

  curve_df <- slab_polys %>%
    dplyr::mutate(y = baseline + sgn * height)

  poly_df <- curve_df %>%
    dplyr::group_by(grp, survey, param, overall_weight) %>%
    dplyr::group_modify(~ rbind(
      data.frame(x = .x$x,      y = .x$y),
      data.frame(x = rev(.x$x), y = rev(.x$baseline))
    )) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  y_labels <- param_label_lookup[ordered_present]
  # Top and bottom page margins are independent fractions of the (uniform) axis
  # spacing.  0.5 => that margin is exactly half the gap between adjacent covariate
  # axes; raise outer_pad_frac_top for headroom above the top (e.g. tall annotations).
  y_lim    <- c(min(pos) - row_spacing * outer_pad_frac_bottom,
                max(pos) + row_spacing * outer_pad_frac_top)
  xq       <- quantile(plot_df$estimate, probs = c(0.005, 0.995), na.rm = TRUE)
  x_lim    <- if (!is.null(x_limits)) x_limits else c(floor(xq[1]), ceiling(xq[2]))

  w_max <- max(poly_df$overall_weight, na.rm = TRUE)

  # Legend: vertically centre it on one covariate's axis (default = 30-day
  # outflow).  Convert that baseline's data-y into panel-normalised [0,1] space,
  # then apply legend_y_nudge to correct for the panel-vs-plot offset.
  legend_baseline <- if (legend_on_param %in% names(pos)) pos[[legend_on_param]] else pos[[1]]
  legend_norm_y   <- (legend_baseline - y_lim[1]) / (y_lim[2] - y_lim[1]) + legend_y_nudge

  # ── Build plot ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Median hash: survey-coloured (median_tick_color = NULL) or a single fixed colour.
  tick_layer <- if (is.null(median_tick_color)) {
    geom_segment(data = annot_rel,
                 aes(x = median_x, xend = median_x,
                     y = baseline, yend = baseline + tick_sgn * median_tick_len,
                     color = survey),
                 linewidth = 0.6, lineend = "round")
  } else {
    geom_segment(data = annot_rel,
                 aes(x = median_x, xend = median_x,
                     y = baseline, yend = baseline + tick_sgn * median_tick_len),
                 color = median_tick_color, linewidth = 0.6, lineend = "round")
  }

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = pos, color = "grey75", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
    geom_polygon(
      data = poly_df,
      aes(x = x, y = y, group = grp, fill = survey, alpha = overall_weight),
      color = NA
    ) +
    geom_path(
      data = curve_df,
      aes(x = x, y = y, group = grp),
      color = "black", linewidth = 0.4
    ) +
    tick_layer

  # Per-model number(weight) annotations — dropped when show_annotations = FALSE (alt5).
  if (isTRUE(show_annotations)) {
    p <- p +
      geom_text(
        data = dplyr::filter(annot_rel, survey == "TPS"),
        aes(x = label_x, y = label_y, label = label_text),
        angle = tps_annot_angle, size = annot_size, family = base_family,
        hjust = tps_annot_hjust, vjust = 0.5, color = "grey20"
      ) +
      geom_text(
        data = dplyr::filter(annot_rel, survey == "EDSM"),
        aes(x = label_x, y = label_y, label = label_text),
        angle = edsm_annot_angle, size = annot_size, family = base_family,
        hjust = edsm_annot_hjust, vjust = 0.5, color = "grey20"
      )
  }

  # Legend labels are rendered by marquee, so bolding is markdown (**TPS**) rather
  # than a `face` argument, which element_marquee does not have.
  legend_lab <- if (identical(legend_text_face, "bold")) {
    function(b) paste0("**", b, "**")
  } else {
    function(b) b
  }

  p <- p +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = y_lim, xlim = x_lim) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = survey_colors, name = NULL,
                      breaks = c("TPS", "EDSM"), labels = legend_lab) +
    scale_color_manual(values = survey_colors, name = NULL, guide = "none") +
    scale_alpha_continuous(range = alpha_range, limits = c(0, w_max), guide = "none") +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = legend_swatch_alpha), ncol = 1)) +
    scale_x_continuous(name = x_axis_label) +
    # expand = 0 on y: no extra padding beyond y_lim, so the top/bottom margins are
    # EXACTLY row_spacing*outer_pad_frac_top/_bottom (default ggplot 5% expansion would otherwise
    # inflate them past the between-axis gap and offset the legend centring).
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = pos, labels = y_labels, name = NULL,
                       expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
    labs(title = title) +
    marquee::marquefy_theme(theme_minimal(base_family = base_family)) +
    theme(
      # marquee renders **bold**.  It ONLY works because marquefy_theme() above also
      # marquee-ises the root text element — ggplot2 4.x element inheritance would
      # otherwise strip the subclass and print the ** literally (as ggtext does).
      # NOTE: line-centring is NOT done here — marquee ignores both `align` and
      # `hjust` for the lines inside a block.  It is baked into the label strings
      # by center_md_lines() in the inputs chunk.
      axis.text.y        = marquee::element_marquee(size = axis_text_y_size, angle = 30,
                                                    hjust = 1, lineheight = 1.05),
      # Must be element_marquee too: with a marquee ROOT text element, a plain
      # element_text child is PROMOTED to marquee and loses its size, so the x tick
      # labels render enormous (the giant "-2024" / "0" bug).
      axis.text.x        = marquee::element_marquee(size = axis_text_x_size),
      axis.title.x       = marquee::element_marquee(size = axis_title_size),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
      legend.position      = c(legend_x, legend_norm_y),
      legend.justification = c(0, 0.5),   # left edge, vertically centred on the target axis
      legend.direction     = "vertical",
      legend.background    = element_rect(fill = alpha("white", 0.6), color = NA),
      # element_marquee has no `face` argument — legend bolding is done by wrapping
      # the legend labels in ** (see legend_lab() above).
      legend.text          = marquee::element_marquee(size = legend_text_size)
    )

  p
}
```

```{r alt4-inputs}
# Extra line breaks so long labels fit the 84 mm column: break AFTER these words.
# (Names are preserved so the b_* -> label lookup still resolves.)
.labels_alt4 <- combined_param_labels
for (.w in c("Distance", "Dissolved", "Emergent", "Terminal"))
  .labels_alt4 <- sub(paste0(.w, " "), paste0(.w, "\n"), .labels_alt4, fixed = TRUE)
# The y-axis is drawn by marquee::element_marquee so "**Edge Type**" renders bold.
# In markdown a lone "\n" is only a SOFT break (renders as a space), so every line
# break must become a HARD break = two trailing spaces before the newline.  Done last,
# so the breaks inserted above are converted too.  combined_param_labels itself is left
# untouched — only this copy is markdown-ised.
# Centre the lines within each block (NBSP padding — see center_md_lines()).
.labels_alt4 <- center_md_lines(.labels_alt4, family = "Helvetica", size = 8.5)
.labels_alt4 <- gsub("\n", "  \n", .labels_alt4, fixed = TRUE)
names(.labels_alt4) <- names(combined_param_labels)

butterfly_forest_alt4_inputs <- list(
  preferred_param_order = combined_preferred_param_order,
  param_labels          = .labels_alt4,
  survey_colors         = combined_survey_colors,
  declutter_threshold   = 0.95,
  min_weight            = 0.01,   # drop <1% models to cut annotation clutter at 84 mm
  x_axis_label          = "Posterior beta estimate (z-score)",
  patterns_to_exclude   = c(combined_patterns_to_exclude, "^b_ph_z$"),
  x_limits      = NULL,

  slab_scale    = 1.5,
  band_half     = 1.5,
  slab_n        = 128L,
  band_gap      = 0.4,

  alpha_range   = c(0.12, 0.85),

  # ── Median hash mark (replaces the dot) ───────────────────────────────────
  median_tick_len = 0.4,   # length of the vertical median tick (band units, into the slab)

  # ── Vertical margins + legend placement ───────────────────────────────────
  outer_pad_frac_top    = 0.64,   # top margin: extra headroom for the vertical outflow annotations
                                  # (= the old 0.55 + 0.3 band-units, expressed as a fraction)
  outer_pad_frac_bottom = 0.55,   # bottom margin = 55% of the uniform axis spacing
                                  # (a bit of extra room for annotation text)
  legend_on_param = "b_out30_z",  # legend centred on the 30-day outflow axis
  legend_x        = 0.02,         # legend left edge (panel-normalised x)
  legend_y_nudge  = 0,            # fine-tune legend vertical centring (+ up / - down)

  # ── Lettering — all held in the 8-9 pt band (E&C floor is 8 pt) ────────────
  base_family      = "Helvetica",
  annot_size       = 2.85,   # ~8.1 pt
  axis_text_y_size = 8.5,
  axis_text_x_size = 8,
  axis_title_size  = 9,
  legend_text_size = 8,

  # ── Annotation controls ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
  annot_x_gap      = 0.35,
  tps_annot_angle  = 90,
  edsm_annot_angle = -90,
  tps_annot_hjust  = 0,
  edsm_annot_hjust = 0,

  tps_annot_x  = 0.75,
  edsm_annot_x = 2,
  tps_annot_y  = 0.4,
  edsm_annot_y = 0.35,

  output_file   = "output_figs/combined_TPS_EDSM_butterfly_forest_alt4_kfold",
  output_width  = 88  / 25.4,   # 88 mm = 3.465 in.  NOTE: E&C's one-column max is 84 mm —
                                # at 88 mm the journal may scale the figure down ~5%, which
                                # would pull the 8 pt lettering under their 8 pt minimum.
                                # but I will be cropping the figure to 84 mm so this won't be a problem
  output_height = 234 / 25.4,   # 234 mm = 9.213 in  (E&C max page height)
  output_dpi    = 600           # combination art (line work + shaded fills) -> 600 dpi
)
```

FIGURE 3c — ALT5: annotation-free butterfly forest (clean variant)
Same geometry as ALT4 (uniform axis spacing, journal-sized, 30-day-outflow-centred legend)
but with the per-model number(weight) annotations DROPPED, the median hash marks recoloured
black and shortened to 75% of the ALT4 length, and a more-saturated, bold legend.  It reuses
the ALT4 function through cosmetic flags, inheriting every other ALT4 setting via modifyList.
```{r alt5-inputs}
butterfly_forest_alt5_inputs <- modifyList(butterfly_forest_alt4_inputs, list(
  show_annotations      = FALSE,   # drop the per-model number(weight) labels
  median_tick_len       = 0.45,    # 75% of ALT4's 0.6
  median_tick_color     = "black", # all median hashes black (not survey-coloured)
  slab_scale            = 1.875,   # 25% taller curves than ALT4's 1.5 (room freed by dropping labels)
  outer_pad_frac_top    = 0.5,    # symmetric top/bottom; >= slab_scale/row_spacing so the taller
  outer_pad_frac_bottom = 0.5,    #   edge slabs don't clip (no annotation headroom needed here)
  legend_swatch_alpha   = 1,       # fully saturated legend colour swatches
  legend_text_face      = "bold",  # bold legend labels
  output_file           = "output_figs/combined_TPS_EDSM_butterfly_forest_alt5_kfold"
))
```

  annot_y               = ri$annot_y,
  annot_hjust           = ri$annot_hjust
)
fl_forest_right
ggsave(paste0(ri$output_file, ".pdf"),  fl_forest_right, device = "pdf",
       width = ri$output_width, height = ri$output_height)
ggsave(paste0(ri$output_file, ".tiff"), fl_forest_right, device = "tiff",
       dpi = ri$output_dpi, compression = "lzw",

FIGURE 5 — Fork-length conditional effects, original-scale x (freed water-year-day y-axis)
```{r fig-fl-ce-origscale, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
# Re-key the b_-named x-axis labels / order to effect-term names (the cached CE list
# is keyed by effect names).  Stripping "b_" is sufficient here (Edge_Type has none).
fl_x_labels <- cond_plot_inputs_fl_origscale$param_labels
names(fl_x_labels) <- sub("^b_", "", names(fl_x_labels))
fl_pref <- sub("^b_", "", cond_plot_inputs_fl_origscale$preferred_param_order_cond)

fl_ce_origscale <- plot_fl_ensemble_ce_cached(
  ensemble_ce_list     = cond_fl$ce_list,
  preferred_order      = fl_pref,
  ncol                 = cond_plot_inputs_fl_origscale$ncol,
  main_title           = cond_plot_inputs_fl_origscale$main_title,
  x_axis_labels        = fl_x_labels,
  y_axis_label         = cond_plot_inputs_fl_origscale$y_axis_label,
  show_facet_subtitles = cond_plot_inputs_fl_origscale$show_facet_subtitles,
  fixed_y_scale        = cond_plot_inputs_fl_origscale$fixed_y_scale,
  # Water year day is a CONTROL (accounted for, not a focal predictor of size) and its
  # ribbon runs down to ~46 mm.  Giving it its own axis keeps the shared range at
  # 57.6-83.8 for the focal panels; folding it in would widen them to 44.6-85.7 and
  # flatten the focal effects.
  free_y_effects       = "water_year_day_z",
  ce_color             = cond_plot_inputs_fl_origscale$ce_color,
  z_stats              = fl_z_stats_origscale
)
fl_ce_origscale
ggsave(paste0(cond_plot_inputs_fl_origscale$output_file, ".pdf"),  fl_ce_origscale, device = "pdf",
       width = cond_plot_inputs_fl_origscale$output_width, height = cond_plot_inputs_fl_origscale$output_height)
ggsave(paste0(cond_plot_inputs_fl_origscale$output_file, ".tiff"), fl_ce_origscale, device = "tiff",
       dpi = cond_plot_inputs_fl_origscale$output_dpi, compression = "lzw",
       width = cond_plot_inputs_fl_origscale$output_width, height = cond_plot_inputs_fl_origscale$output_height)
```
